newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index edges up 0.36 pts in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index edges up 0.36 pts in dull trade.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mostly flat in thin trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with the SAX index firming 0.36 points to 201.91.

Brokers said the current sluggish mood on the floor may be the "silence before the storm", as there were signals on the over-the-counter market indicating possible higher interest among investors in near future.
Both oil and gas storage company Nafta and shipbuilder Slovenske Lodenice did not trade on the BSE floor, but were active in OTC trading brokers said.

Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB was the only blue chip to move from its Wednesday close, losing 10 crowns and to 1,740. But only 30 shares traded in the bank, making it hard for brokers to predict future development with VUB price.
Steel maker VSZ and oil refiner Slovnaft closed both unchanged at 630 and 910 crowns respectively, with 178 shares and 117 shares changing hands.

"While the market is waiting for new investors bringing the fresh mood on the floor, the investors appeared to have been waiting for further falls in prices of all main issues before they buy new shares," said Jozef Cimra of ING Barings.
Overall volume decreased to 163,704 shares, from 389,956 shares traded on Thursday, turnover fell to 136.62 million crowns, from 179.2 million.
